key_insight: Menopausal timing showed a nonlinear association with blood NfL and a linear association with GDF-15 in older women, providing observational evidence relevant to dementia biology—not AI cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: These findings may inform research into menopause-related dementia vulnerability but do not establish causality or support clinical risk prediction.
method: Observational analysis of the U.S. Health and Retirement Study using blood collected in 2016.
Modeled self-reported spontaneous menopause timing against four blood biomarkers, adjusting for sociodemographic and health factors.
Evaluated APOE ε4 effect modification and separately examined hysterectomy history.
evidence_signal: Among 893 women without hysterectomy, later menopause between ages 50–55 was associated with lower NfL (−0.031 SD/year; 95% CI −0.051 to −0.011); overall, later menopause was associated with lower GDF-15, while GFAP and p-tau181 associations were not significant.
watch_item: The supplied abstract is truncated, and self-reported reproductive history plus observational biomarker associations cannot establish effects on subsequent dementia risk.
paper_title: Age at Menopause and Dementia Risk: Blood-Based Biomarker Evidence from a US National Study
